draw.note: Designation (parent): Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks World Heritage Site, Jasper National Park. Named among the views of the Sulphur Skyline trail in the park's hiking guide; no wider fame found.

standing.note: One of several ridges seen from the trail.

distinction.note: Many ridges of the Miette Range look alike.

easy_payoff.note: Only the walkers who reach the summit see it well.

weather.note: A view from a summit needs a clear day.

records.why: A Miette Range ridge in Jasper, seen from the Sulphur Skyline trail above Miette Hot Springs.

v.note: the view is from the Sulphur Skyline summit, 4.4 km and 700 m up
Miette Road closed mid-October to mid-May

wikidata.note: agent-checked 2026-10-28 (travel-researcher): label 'Athabasca Glacier', instance of glacier, P625 0.35 km from OSM relation 19256027; needs a person's check

draw.note: Designation (parent): Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks World Heritage Site, Jasper National Park. Parks Canada calls it one of the world's most accessible glaciers, seen by millions.

standing.note: The best-known glacier toe in the Rockies.

distinction.note: Few glaciers this large reach so close to a highway.

easy_payoff.note: The view is from the lot or a 1.8 km return walk.

weather.note: Wind and cloud often sit on the icefield.

records.why: The most visited glacier tongue of the Columbia Icefield, a short walk from the Icefields Parkway.

access_cost.note: No access cost beyond the park entry or vehicle pass, which the park's requirement offers carry.
